forecast_candidates.rationale: BTC has positive 12h and 24h returns, improving breadth, positive spot depth and taker imbalances, but mixed cross-horizon behavior, negative 4h return, declining open interest, neutral sentiment and negative aggregate aggressive flow. A bounded continuation/consolidation range is more consistent with the supplied disagreement than a directional breakout claim.

ETH has stronger 24h performance and persistent ETH/BTC strength, but the latest order-book imbalance is sharply negative, ETH funding rose materially alongside higher open interest, and the 4h return was negative. These opposing signals support a wide unratified range candidate rather than a clean directional forecast.

A conditional downside candidate is supported by the sharp deterioration in ETH depth imbalance, negative latest taker imbalance, higher funding with rising open interest, and negative 4h ETH/BTC return. This is counterbalanced by positive 12h/24h returns and 168 consecutive ETH/BTC closes above 0.03, so it remains low-conviction and unratified.

The most material change is a sharp breadth rebound from 26% to 59% advancers alongside positive BTC and ETH price changes, but this improvement is not fully confirmed by rotation or positioning data. ETH shows the clearest internal tension: persistent ETH/BTC strength and positive 24h performance coexist with sharply negative latest depth imbalance, negative 4h relative performance, materially higher funding and modestly rising open interest. BTC has healthier spot microstructure, but declining open interest, negative 4h performance and negative aggressive-flow aggregates temper the continuation case. Overall, the evidence is more consistent with an advancing but fragile transition or pause than with confirmed broad rotation; late-cycle deterioration risk is rising but not established. The phase and warning are descriptive shadow interpretations only, and the forecast candidates are unratified research objects.
